sources.entry: chasquid - SMTP (email) server with a focus on simplicity, security, and ease of operation. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go

summary.name: chasquid
summary.one_liner: chasquid is an SMTP (email) server written in Go, designed as a simple, secure mail transfer agent for individuals and small groups.
use_cases: running a mail server for a small group
hosting multiple email domains with aliases
summary.what_it_does: chasquid sends and receives email as a typical MTA and can be used in place of Postfix or Exim. It supports multiple virtual domains with per-domain users and aliases, and drops suffixes so user+something@domain delivers to user@domain. It tracks per-domain TLS support to prevent connection downgrading, supports multiple TLS certificates, and integrates with Let's Encrypt. It performs SPF and MTA-STS checks and offers hooks for greylisting, anti-virus, anti-spam, and DKIM/DMARC. A monitoring HTTP server exposes variables and tracing for debugging.
notable: Hard to misconfigure insecurely (no open relay, no clear-text auth)
Tracks per-domain TLS support and prevents connection downgrading
Supports SMTPUTF8 and IDNA international names
caveats: Designed mainly for individuals and small groups rather than large-scale deployments
Platform integrations named are Debian, Ubuntu, and Arch
